title: Data tables: records, fields and filters
p: A data table keeps records that share the same fields: books you are reading, feedback you collect, a list of contacts. Each field has a type, so a date stays a date and a rating stays a number of stars. For a table to try, open {{doc:reading-list}} in this folder.

ul.li: Choose Data table from the New menu of a folder. The table is a .sqlite file of its own in your documents folder.
In a page, type /data and choose Data table to put one inside the page. Hover over it and choose Full screen to give it the whole window.
Edit a cell: click it and type, or press Enter. Tab and the arrow keys move between cells.
Add a record: click Add record at the top left, or the plus below the last row; right-click a row to insert one above or below it.
Open a record: click the expand control at the start of a row, or right-click it and choose Open record, to see and edit every field at once.
Add a field: click the plus control after the last column, name it and pick its type.
Change a field: click a column header and choose Edit field to rename it or change its type. Existing values are converted where they can be.

td.p: Typed values with their own formats
Choose from options; each option has a color
A calendar picker, a tick box, stars
Links that open, and files kept with the table
A value computed from other fields, such as {Price} * {Quantity}
Each cell is a page of its own: click an empty cell and choose New note, or point it to an existing note
Auto number, Date created, Last modified time

p: The tools at the top right filter, sort and group the records, choose which fields show, set the row height and color rows; Search records finds text in any cell. A column header's menu offers the same for that field: Filter by this field, Sort A to Z, Group by this field, or Hide field.

callout.p: Filters, sorts and groups change what you see, not the records. Clear them to see every record again.

ul.li: Select cells and copy them: they paste into a spreadsheet as rows and columns, or into another table.
Paste rows from a spreadsheet or a CSV file into a table to add them.
The … menu at the top right exports the table as CSV or copies it as a Markdown table.

p: Every data table is a plain SQLite database: each table is an SQL table under its own name, with the fields as columns and the values you see. Other tools, scripts and agents can read and change it without knowing Quiet.md; it picks up their changes the next time it reads the file.
